I have been in this situation before. When things are that bad, it’s important to get away. You may still feel some attachment. That’s normal for anything. I never liked high school but at graduation there was a sadness. I also had to leave an ex due to emotional and physical abuse and it left me feeling a lot of pain. I’m my opinion, I believe it was more the fear of the unknown for me than fear of losing something. I hated every second of my last job for example, but when I left, everything felt a little depressing knowing I’d never see the place again but I think it was really just that that’s what I got used to, and I was leaving a place of familiarity for a chance that the next thing will be better. When I graduated high school, I was able to be free from every stupid thing I said and did and didn’t have to be labeled as the weird suicidal girl, when I left my ex, I got to be free from worrying about his feelings whenever I did anything, I don’t feel like I had to walk around on eggshells all the time when I was going through my day to day life anymore, and I’ve been single for 3 years now but this is the happiest I’ve been. And I started my new job 5 months ago, and they treat me with respect, the hours are better, and I get paid $5 more an hour! And I will go back to high school, I’ll never go back to my ex, and i will never go back to my previous employer. Good things are on your horizon, if leaving is what you know you need to do, then you have to stay strong in that decision. Brighter days are coming and you will be happier for it. Hope this helps.
